provenance.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
provenance.source_document_title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
exact_source_references.source_document_title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.6 — clinical history, examination, objective tests, and occupational asthma
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports wheeze, cough, breathlessness, chest tightness, symptom variation, nocturnal or seasonal pattern, triggers, atopy and family history, occupational context, respiratory examination, peak flow, FeNO, spirometry, and objective confirmation.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
exact_source_references.source_document_title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.5.1–1.6.4 — monitoring asthma control and uncontrolled asthma
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports review of symptoms, time off work or school, reliever use, systemic steroid courses, admissions or emergency attendance, validated control questionnaires, peak flow, FeNO, adherence, inhaler technique, smoking or vaping, occupational, psychosocial, seasonal and environmental factors, and response to treatment change.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
exact_source_references.source_document_title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.11.1 and 1.14.1–1.14.2 — inhaler technique, adherence, and action plans
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports inhaler-technique and adherence review at every review and clinician-documented personalised action-plan and trigger discussion without mapping medicine names or doses.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Thoracic Society
exact_source_references.source_document_title: British Thoracic Society Clinical Statement on chronic cough in adults

exact_section.heading: Scope and definition of chronic cough
exact_section.evidence_summary: Defines chronic cough in adults as cough lasting more than 8 weeks and sets the statement scope.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Thoracic Society
exact_source_references.source_document_title: British Thoracic Society Clinical Statement on chronic cough in adults

exact_section.heading: Clinical history and examination
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports cough duration and character, sputum, smoking, medicines, occupation and environment, wheeze, rhinitis, heartburn, functional and mood impact, and face-to-face upper-airway, ear and chest examination.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Thoracic Society
exact_source_references.source_document_title: British Thoracic Society Clinical Statement on chronic cough in adults

exact_section.heading: Basic investigations and referral
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports chest radiography, spirometry with reversibility, sputum testing where infection is suspected, selected inflammatory markers, specialist referral for persistent or unclear cough, and upper-airway specialist assessment when indicated.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology
exact_source_references.source_document_title: BSACI guideline for the diagnosis and management of allergic and non-allergic rhinitis (Revised Edition 2017; First edition 2007)

exact_section.heading: Sections 7.1–7.10 — history, triggers, symptom pattern, impact, and contextual factors
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports documenting onset, duration, triggers, rhinorrhoea, obstruction, sneezing, itching, crusting, eye and lower-airway symptoms, sleep, snoring, mouth breathing, family, social, occupational, and medicine context without assigning rhinitis subtype.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology
exact_source_references.source_document_title: BSACI guideline for the diagnosis and management of allergic and non-allergic rhinitis (Revised Edition 2017; First edition 2007)

exact_section.heading: Sections 8.1–8.3 — visual, nasal, oral, and upper-airway examination
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-performed general inspection, mouth-breathing observation, airflow assessment, anterior rhinoscopy, secretions, septal appearance, polyps, crusting, throat, and postnasal-drip documentation.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology
exact_source_references.source_document_title: BSACI guideline for the diagnosis and management of allergic and non-allergic rhinitis (Revised Edition 2017; First edition 2007)

exact_section.heading: Sections 9.1–9.8 — allergy testing and investigation context
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports recording clinician-selected allergy testing and already available specialist or imaging results; routine radiology and autonomous testing are not mapped.

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.4.6 — clinical history, examination, objective tests, and occupational asthma
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports wheeze, cough, breathlessness, chest tightness, symptom variation, nocturnal or seasonal pattern, triggers, atopy and family history, occupational context, respiratory examination, peak flow, FeNO, spirometry, and objective confirmation.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
exact_source_references.source_document_title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.5.1–1.6.4 — monitoring asthma control and uncontrolled asthma
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports review of symptoms, time off work or school, reliever use, systemic steroid courses, admissions or emergency attendance, validated control questionnaires, peak flow, FeNO, adherence, inhaler technique, smoking or vaping, occupational, psychosocial, seasonal and environmental factors, and response to treatment change.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
exact_source_references.source_document_title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.11.1 and 1.14.1–1.14.2 — inhaler technique, adherence, and action plans
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports inhaler-technique and adherence review at every review and clinician-documented personalised action-plan and trigger discussion without mapping medicine names or doses.

exact_source_references.source_document_title: British Thoracic Society Clinical Statement on chronic cough in adults

exact_section.heading: Scope and definition of chronic cough
exact_section.evidence_summary: Defines chronic cough in adults as cough lasting more than 8 weeks and sets the statement scope.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Thoracic Society
exact_source_references.source_document_title: British Thoracic Society Clinical Statement on chronic cough in adults

exact_section.heading: Clinical history and examination
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports cough duration and character, sputum, smoking, medicines, occupation and environment, wheeze, rhinitis, heartburn, functional and mood impact, and face-to-face upper-airway, ear and chest examination.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Thoracic Society
exact_source_references.source_document_title: British Thoracic Society Clinical Statement on chronic cough in adults

exact_section.heading: Basic investigations and referral
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports chest radiography, spirometry with reversibility, sputum testing where infection is suspected, selected inflammatory markers, specialist referral for persistent or unclear cough, and upper-airway specialist assessment when indicated.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology
exact_source_references.source_document_title: BSACI guideline for the diagnosis and management of allergic and non-allergic rhinitis (Revised Edition 2017; First edition 2007)

exact_section.heading: Sections 7.1–7.10 — history, triggers, symptom pattern, impact, and contextual factors
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports documenting onset, duration, triggers, rhinorrhoea, obstruction, sneezing, itching, crusting, eye and lower-airway symptoms, sleep, snoring, mouth breathing, family, social, occupational, and medicine context without assigning rhinitis subtype.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology
exact_source_references.source_document_title: BSACI guideline for the diagnosis and management of allergic and non-allergic rhinitis (Revised Edition 2017; First edition 2007)

exact_section.heading: Sections 8.1–8.3 — visual, nasal, oral, and upper-airway examination
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician-performed general inspection, mouth-breathing observation, airflow assessment, anterior rhinoscopy, secretions, septal appearance, polyps, crusting, throat, and postnasal-drip documentation.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology
exact_source_references.source_document_title: BSACI guideline for the diagnosis and management of allergic and non-allergic rhinitis (Revised Edition 2017; First edition 2007)

exact_section.heading: Sections 9.1–9.8 — allergy testing and investigation context
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports recording clinician-selected allergy testing and already available specialist or imaging results; routine radiology and autonomous testing are not mapped.
